prompt.context: Our client is an Italian pharmaceutical company. They have the right to sell a cardiovascular drug that was developed and previously sold by a multinational pharmaceutical company in the Italian market. The multinational company is leaving the Italian market and gave the rights to sell this drug to our client based on a royalty. The drug regulates blood pressure and has 5 competitors (substitutes) in the market. Sales reps simply go to physicians and illustrate features of the drugs; physicians decide which drugs to prescribe.
prompt.question: Our client has asked us to size the field force (sales reps) needed to reach physicians.

clarifying_info.q: What do the sales reps actually do?
clarifying_info.a: Sales reps go to physicians and illustrate features of the drugs. Physicians decide which drugs to prescribe.

clarifying_info.q: How many physicians prescribe cardiovascular drugs in Italy?
clarifying_info.a: There are 50,000 physicians who prescribe cardiovascular drugs.

clarifying_info.q: How many visits can a sales rep make per day, and how many days do they work per year?
clarifying_info.a: A sales rep can do 7 visits per day and works 200 days per year.

exhibits.title: Physician Visit Frequency Matrix
exhibits.shows: A 2x2 matrix with market share on the Y-axis (Low to High) and number of potential cardiovascular patients in the region on the X-axis (Low to High). Candidates are asked to place physician groups A, B, and C into quadrants.

data.y_axis: Client market share in region (L to H)
data.x_axis: Number of potential cardiovascular patients in region (L to H)

exhibits.title: Percentage of Physicians by Matrix Quadrant
exhibits.shows: The same 2x2 matrix from Figure 1, now filled with the percentage of the 50,000 total cardiovascular physicians that fall into each cell of the matrix.

data.cell_percentages: Reading left-to-right, bottom-to-top: bottom-left=20%, bottom-right=10%, middle-left=30%, middle-right=40%, top-left=40%, top-right=30%, top-right-corner=10% — cells sum across the matrix; key A-type cells are in the high-patients/low-share region

framework: Market Size and Competition: overall market size, growth, client's market share vs. competitors, characteristics of cardiovascular patient population
Activities of the Sales Force: during visit (product features, answering physician questions), before/after visit (prioritization, appointment scheduling)

Patterns Related to Physicians: number and type of physicians (GPs vs. specialists), decision-making process (other stakeholders such as insurers), correlation between visit frequency and probability of prescribing client's drug

questions.prompt: If all regions are plotted on Figure 1 (X = potential cardiovascular patients, Y = client market share), where would you place physician groups A (10 visits/year), B (5 visits/year), and C (2 visits/year)?
questions.guidance: A-type (highest visit frequency) should go to the southeast quadrant: high patient potential but low current market share — greatest upside from rep visits. C-type (lowest visit frequency) should go to the north: high current market share already — marginal gain from additional visits is low. B-type fills the remainder, with the most reps concentrated near the center of the matrix.

questions.prompt: Using Figure 2, calculate how many A-type physicians there are and how many visits per year will be made to them.
questions.guidance: Identify which cells of the matrix are A-type (high patient potential, low market share — southeast). Sum the physician percentages in those cells against the total of 50,000 physicians, then multiply by 10 visits/year.

math.setup: Total physicians = 50,000. Identify A-type cells as the bottom row (low market share). Bottom row = 20% of 50,000 = 10,000 physicians. Of these, the far-right cell (highest patient potential) = 10% of 10,000 = 1,000 physicians. The adjacent cells also classified A-type yield additional physicians; the casebook solution sums to 6,500 A-type physicians total.
steps: Bottom row (low market share) = 20% x 50,000 = 10,000 physicians
Southeast cell = 10% of bottom row = 10% x 10,000 = 1,000 physicians
Adding the other A-type cells across the matrix gives a total of 6,500 A-type physicians
Annual visits to A-type = 6,500 x 10 = 65,000 visits/year
math.answer: 6,500 A-type physicians; 65,000 visits per year to A-type physicians

questions.prompt: Assume total required visits across all physician types is 270,000 per year. How many sales reps does the client need?
questions.guidance: Ask for (or be given) rep productivity assumptions: visits per day and working days per year. Divide total required visits by annual capacity per rep.

math.setup: Total required visits = 270,000/year. Rep capacity = 7 visits/day x 200 working days/year = 1,400 visits/rep/year.
steps: Number of reps = 270,000 / 1,400 ≈ 193, rounded to approximately 200

recommendation: The client needs approximately 200 sales reps to adequately cover the Italian cardiovascular drug market
Reps should be concentrated in high-patient-potential, low-market-share regions (A-type) to maximize prescriptions generated per visit
risks: Actual physician visit conversion rates may differ from model assumptions
Competitor sales forces may respond with increased visit frequency, eroding gains
Royalty structure with the multinational may compress margins if field-force costs are high
next_steps: Validate total required visits figure (270,000) with bottom-up physician segmentation across all matrix cells
Model the revenue impact of proposed market share gains to confirm ROI of the 200-rep field force
Design rep incentive structures tied to market share improvement in A-type regions
